page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-6 is a graphics-optimized server instance featuring an x86_64 CPU architecture with 6 dedicated vCPUs and 22.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.67 GB of memory per core. The instance is equipped with a fractional GPU allocation consisting of 1/8 of an NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage.

The g4-standard-6 instance provides an entry-level access point for GPU-accelerated workloads by utilizing a fractional GPU slice rather than a full dedicated card. This resource density model offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require GPU acceleration but do not saturate a full GPU. Tradeoffs include the lack of local storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which may require additional network configuration and resource provisioning.

This server configuration is designed for workloads such as entry-level graphics rendering, low-intensity machine learning inference, remote workstation hosting, and development environments requiring GPU acceleration.
